chunks: And ponder the conditions of the believers who passed before you,
What was their state during purification and trial?
Were they not the most burdened of creatures, the most exhausted of servants in trial, and those with the narrowest circumstances in the world?!
The Pharaohs took them as slaves, so they treated them with the worst punishment, and made them taste bitterness,
So their condition did not cease to be in the humiliation of ruin and the compulsion of conquest,
finding no means of escape and no way to defend themselves,
until when Allah noticed their earnest patience from them regarding the harm, in their love for Him, and their endurance of the disliked, out of fear of Him,
He provided for them a way out from the straits of trial,
so He replaced their humiliation with honor, and safety with fear,
so they became ruling kings and prominent leaders,
and the honor from Allah reached them to a degree that their own hopes had not reached.
ai.seo_question: How did Allah reward the patience of the believers during their trials?
ai.summary: In the context of Nahj al-Balagha’s sermons on spiritual vigilance, Imam Ali uses the historical archetype of the Israelites under Pharaoh to illustrate the transformative power of *sabr* (patient endurance) amidst severe tribulation. This narrative serves as a theological precedent for the Shia understanding of how divine favor (*karamah*) is earned through steadfastness in affliction, ultimately leading to political and spiritual ascendancy as foretold in the Quran.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Think about the condition of people from among the believers who passed before you.
What distresses and trials they were in!
Were they not the most over-burdened among all the people and in the most straitened circumstances in the whole world?
The Pharaohs took them as slaves. They inflicted on them the worst punishments and bitter sufferings.
They continuously remained in this state of ruinous disgrace and severe subjugation.
They found no method for escape and no way for protection.
Till when Allāh, the Glorified, noticed that they were enduring troubles in His love and bearing distresses out of fear for Him,
He provided escape from the distress of trials.
So, He changed their disgrace into honour and fear into safety.
Consequently, they became ruling kings and conspicuous leaders
and Allāh’s favours over them reached limits to which their own wishes had not reached.
